answer: Flooding registration pushes an hostile operator to the back of the ridge queue while genuine members promoted earlier goes on earning. Admission is quota-limited: at most 597 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the nadir. The canyon index is deterministic from ledger replay, which means nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
